caption:
Google is rolling out Personal Intelligence for Gemini on Android Auto.
With your permission, it pulls from Gmail, Calendar, Photos and Maps to answer questions on the road, like whether your flight is on time.
It is opt-in and can be turned off anytime.

Would you let your car's AI read your email?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: TechCrunch · Photo: Google

slides.headline: Google's Gemini can now dig through *your Gmail and Photos* while you drive

image.generate: Vertical photo from the back seat of a car driving on a city highway at dusk. A man in his thirties at the wheel, seen from slightly behind and to the side in the right two thirds of the frame, glances with a surprised smile at a phone mounted on the dashboard like the car screen in the first image. The phone screen shows a blank colorful assistant interface with soft blue and purple shapes, and floating around it, like a surreal cloud, are small blank paper envelopes, printed photographs and a paper calendar page, as if his personal life is pouring out of the screen. City lights through the windshield, plenty of headroom above his head. The left third of the frame is empty dark car interior. The bottom third is the dark dashboard. Blank surfaces, no readable text or labels on any object, no letters, no logos, no watermarks. Photorealistic, high contrast, one clear subject, vertical composition. It must look like an unedited real photo from a news agency, not a painting, not digital art, no glow effects.

slides.heading: Ask it *like a person*
paras: Google began rolling out Personal Intelligence for Gemini on Android Auto on Tuesday. It can pull from Gmail, Calendar, Photos, Maps, YouTube and Search.
Ask for your flight gate and whether it's on time, and it answers both.

slides.heading: Your photos become *directions*
paras: It can find a car wash from a photo you took last week and take you there, or head to a coffee shop you talked about the day before.
It can also suggest restaurants on your route that fit your tastes.

slides.heading: Off *until you say yes*
paras: It is opt-in: you pick which apps to connect and can switch it off anytime in Gemini settings.
It works on personal accounts for adults 18 and up, not in the EU or UK. Cars with Google built-in get it in the coming months.

slides.hook: Your car is turning into an assistant that knows your life. Follow so you know what it can do next.
